content.text:
I've submitted **index 26** (Sb fraction 0.757) as the best composition, but the EQE differences I measured are all at noise level, so it isn't clearly better than the others.

I used all 5 EQE measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.18 | 0.00005 |
| 13 | 0.38 | −0.00004 |
| 19 | 0.56 | 0.00007 |
| 23 | 0.67 | 0.00016 |
| **26** | **0.76** | **0.00025** |

- **Why it's so low:** the magnesium–antimony oxides in the database are expected to have wide band gaps (about 4 eV or more for MgSb₂O₆), so they absorb almost none of the 2.4 eV light. Magnesium itself doesn't absorb light, so this whole composition line is essentially photo-inactive.
- **Why index 26:** readings went up slightly toward the antimony-rich end, so I spent the last measurements there. Index 26, the most antimony-rich composition on the line, gave the highest value. That may come from a small amount of absorption by antimony oxide or defects, but I didn't check this.
- **Unmeasured:** 22 of the 27 compositions were never measured. The best one on the line could be one of those, though with so little light absorbed any gain is likely to be tiny.
